groups.label: Shield Wall
groups.countReason: two walls (Shield Wall's 'Limit 2 active Shield Walls', gem lookup) shattered together by one Fortifying Cry or Thunderous Leap: two hits land, but only the top bleed applies (one bleed per enemy; the brainstorm gate's interview, interviews/brainstorm-1.md), which the record's Count rule follows by counting the hit twice and the bleed once

boss.note: Raise two Shield Walls beside the boss, then Thunderous Leap onto it: the slam shatters both walls (two hits, one bleed, 140% more) and detonates any Rapid Assault spearheads. Swap to Saitha's Spear and stab with Rapid Assault to aggravate the wall's bleed and leave a spearhead, swap back, raise the next pair. Fortifying Cry shatters a pair whenever its 8 s cooldown is up, triggering Shield Wave and granting Guard. Rake fills the gaps. One bleed per enemy, only the top one deals damage: the wall's bleed while it runs, Rake's in the gaps, never the sum; shattering one wall at a time with Leap refreshes the bleed where a pair adds only a second hit

earned.uptime: map packs walk and run at you while Rake's bleed ticks on them, so most of a bleed counts as moving (an estimate); a pack that stops loses the extra 100% unless Herald of Blood's 59% aggravation lands; on a standing boss the same 100% comes from aggravation, Saitha's Spear's Rapid Assault stabs
Brutality III's 20% chance per hit to ignore physical damage reduction, averaged over hits as PoB does by default

3 Rage per melee hit on each enemy struck (Bestial Rage and its two Rage on Hit small passives), so the 30 cap fills in a pack's first strikes and holds while you keep hitting; it starts draining 4 s after the last hit (BaseRageLossDelayMs 4000), so a long walk between packs restarts it

customMods.reason: Shield Wall's '100% more Damage if destroyed by your Skills' plus 40% from its 20% quality (gem lookup 'Shield Wall'; Data/Skills/act_str.lua), which PoB has no stat map for (check_model_coverage gems Shield Wall: possibly unmodelled); every wall here is shattered by Fortifying Cry or Thunderous Leap, your own Warcry and Slam, so the line holds on each wall; the 80% less when an enemy breaks it inside 0.5 s is left out, a risk

Rake's own 'Deals up to 130% more Damage, based on the distance travelled' (100% plus 30% from 20% quality; gem lookup 'Rake'), which PoB applies none of: its stat map names base_dash_additional_damage_from_distance_+%_final while the gem carries base_additional_damage_from_distance_+%_final (Data/Skills/act_dex.lua:6428-6442; the card's skill-shape probe, check 8). Worked out on PoB's own ramp for the line, full at 50 units (5 m, the dash's base_melee_dash_range 50), at PoB's default enemy distance of 20 units (Modules/ConfigOptions.lua:1621): 20/50 x 130% = 52%. A dash from further pays up to 130%, one from beside the enemy nothing

Momentum's 'After moving at least 2 metres during a single use of a Supported Skill, the rest of that use deals 40% more Damage' (gem lookup 'Momentum'), which PoB never applies to Rake: its config option 'Moved 2m during Skill use?' shows only for skills usable while moving (Modules/ConfigOptions.lua:484), and Rake isn't one (the card's dead-slot audit, check 5). Rake's slash comes after its dash, so a dash of 2 m or more earns the 40%; at the 2 m average the distance line above assumes, about half the uses reach it: 40% x 0.5 = 20% (an estimate; needs in-game testing)

claims.text: Tribal Fury (750) carries the clear: its 'Strikes deal Splash Damage' makes Rake, a Strike, hit the target's neighbours, and each splash hit leaves Blood Loss through Atziri's Acuity for the Heralds' explosions. PoB ignores the line, so node power counts the notable as travel; the splash's gain is unmeasured and needs in-game testing.

source.ref: check_model_coverage nodes 750 ([unparsed] Strikes deal Splash Damage); lookup_game_data gem "Rake" (tags: Strike)

claims.text: Bestial Rage (10873) and its two Rage on Hit passives (47790, 17625) supply the 30 Rage the configuration counts on: 1 Rage on Melee Hit each, 3 a hit, and Bestial Rage's 12% increased Physical Damage per 10 Rage. Node power can't see the supply, because the Rage count is an earned configuration value that stays set without the nodes.

source.ref: check_model_coverage nodes 47790, 17625, 10873 (Gain 1 Rage on Melee Hit; Every 10 Rage also grants 12% increased Physical Damage)

claims.text: The nine attribute passives set to Dexterity hold the Dexterity that Rake, Thunderous Leap and Rapid Assault require, reached only with the gear's Dexterity lines beside them; node power ranks damage and life alone, so it would move these points and leave the requirement unmet.

The twenty-seven attribute passives set to Strength hold the Strength that Shield Wall, Fortifying Cry and the armour bases require; node power ranks damage and life alone, so it would move these points and leave the requirements unmet.

Blood Magic (51749) turns every skill's mana cost into a life cost, so Rake's cost per second comes out of life, which Atziri's Acuity's leech refills while hits land; without it Rake's cost outruns the mana the build regenerates and leeches, a sustain node power doesn't measure.

Take the Titan points in this order: Life Regeneration, Mysterious Lineage, Strength, Colossal Capacity, Strength, Hulking Form. Life Regeneration is the small passive on the way in; Mysterious Lineage (15% more maximum life) is the first notable, the pool that meets the hardest hits; the two Strength passives (4% increased Strength each) and Colossal Capacity (an inventory chest, no combat value) are the path to Hulking Form, whose 50% increased effect of small passives reaches the bleed and ailment small passives.
Act 2, Valley of the Titans, the Medallion: take 30% increased Charm Charges Gained with its +1 Charm Slot; both options give the slot, and the faster charges keep the charms going through a map.
Act 3, Venom Crypts, the Venom Draught: take 25% increased Stun Threshold, for a melee build that stands in the pack; the mana regeneration option does nothing once Blood Magic leaves no mana.

Act 4, Eye of Hinekora, Tribal Medicine: take 30% increased Global Armour, Evasion and Energy Shield, more of the armour the hardest physical hits meet; the other option's armour applying to elemental damage repeats the body armour's line, and its deflection and energy shield parts give this build nothing.
Act 4, Halls of the Dead, Tawhoa's Test: take +5% to Lightning Resistance over +5 Dexterity, toward the capped resistances the endgame needs.
Act 4, Halls of the Dead, Tasalio's Test: take +5% to Cold Resistance over +5 Intelligence, which no gem or item here needs.
Act 4, Halls of the Dead, Ngamahu's Test: take +5% to Fire Resistance over +5 Strength, toward the capped resistances the endgame needs.

Act 4, Abandoned Prison, the Goddess of Justice: take 30% increased Life Recovery from Flasks; neither option helps much here, since Blood Magic leaves no mana and Vaal Pact (see the gloves' trap) recovers life from leech alone, and the life option serves a player who later drops Atziri's Acuity.
Interlude 2, Qimah, the Seven Pillars: take +5% to all Elemental Resistances, the most resistance any option gives, toward the capped resistances the endgame needs.

PoB's support ranking puts Hourglass first for Rake, with Excise, Execrate and Expanse alike; Rake takes Brutality III, Heavy Swing and Ancestral Call II instead, because each of those four gives the supported skill a cooldown (8 to 10 seconds), which the skill used on every pack can't carry, and PoB's bleed figure, rated per bleed, never sees the cooldown.

source.ref: lookup_game_data mechanic "Supported Skills have a Cooldown" (Excise, Execrate, Expanse: 8 seconds; Hourglass: 10 seconds)

claims.text: PoB measures nothing from Momentum on Rake: its 'Moved 2m during Skill use?' option shows only for skills usable while moving, and Rake isn't one. Momentum stays, since Rake's slash follows its dash, and a 20% custom modifier stands for its 40% more on about half the uses; that share needs in-game testing.

Crit stays unpulled: 60% increased critical hit chance with a 30% critical damage bonus added 16% to Rake on a budget-rung probe, but it takes two suffixes that the resistance caps, the amulet's melee levels and the Dexterity lines already hold.

source.ref: D1-build's probe on b (pieces.md, row cr2-s-1-16)

claims.text: A reliable shock stays unpulled: Thunderous Leap is the only lightning hit, its shock on a Pinnacle boss isn't measured, and the leap's turn in the boss cycle is spent shattering the walls.

source.ref: D1-build's lever check: no other lightning source in the skill groups; the boss rotation (skills.boss)

claims.text: Exposure stays unpulled: it lowers an enemy's elemental resistances, and the damage here, the bleeds and the hits that make them, is physical.

source.ref: lookup_game_data gem "Rake" (tags: Physical); lookup_game_data gem "Shield Wall" (tags: Physical)

claims.text: Curses stay unpulled: Vulnerability, the armour curse, makes hits ignore armour, which the bleeds don't meet, and it needs 137 Intelligence at gem level 18 and 157 at 20, far beyond what this Strength and Dexterity build carries.

Bleed duration stays thin, Lasting Trauma's 20% and the jewels' lines only: Scent of Blood and the Bleed Duration small passives, which the card planned on, unlock only with the Oracle's The Unseen Path, so a Titan can't take them.

source.ref: the card's structure check (cards/r2-s-1.md, Found while pathing): nodes 60014, 8248 and 48079 unlock with The Unseen Path (5571)

claims.text: Spirit is left partly free: War Banner, the obvious taker, waits on 200 Glory and a press every 10 seconds, a third button in a boss cycle already full, so it isn't taken.

Saitha's Spear sits on weapon set 2 for bosses only: its (25-40)% chance to Aggravate Bleeding on Hit gives the wall's bleed on a standing boss the extra 100% that moving packs give for free, and keeping it off set 1 leaves Rake the rare spear's damage.

Rapid Assault is bound to weapon set 2 alone: after each shatter, swap, use it once for Saitha's aggravation and the spearheads, and swap back; the boss estimate counts its hits and gives its bleed only the gaps the wall's bleed leaves.
Thunderous Leap, a Slam and a Detonator, both shatters the walls where it lands and explodes the spearheads Rapid Assault left, once a boss cycle; the boss estimate counts that explosion.

Crushing Impacts, the card's fourth Titan notable, is left out: the eight ascendancy points go to Mysterious Lineage, Hulking Form and Stone Skin, and its 25% more pays only against heavy-stunned enemies, which nothing here builds.

source.ref: search_tree_nodes {ascendancy: "Titan"} (Crushing Impacts: 25% more Damage against Heavy Stunned Enemies)

claims.text: Atziri's Acuity brings Vaal Pact: life recovers only from leech, so no life flask or regeneration works, and life comes back only while hits land; the bleeds, which deal most of the damage, are damage over time and leech nothing (judgment).

source.ref: check_model_coverage nodes Vaal Pact (33369): Cannot Recover Life other than from Leech; lookup_game_data unique "Atziri's Acuity"

claims.text: A Shield Wall an enemy breaks within 0.5 seconds deals 80% less; the 100% more (140% at 20% quality) comes only when your own Slam, Warcry or Shield Charge shatters it, so shatter each pair with Thunderous Leap or Fortifying Cry as soon as it stands.

Under Blood Magic every skill costs life, and life returns only through the gloves' leech: each wall raised before anything is hit costs its life cost with nothing to refill it, so open on a pack or a boss with Rake or the leap.

Entering maps, buy in this order toward the 5-divine total: Atziri's Acuity first (the Blood Loss loop and the only life recovery), then the spear with +2 melee levels, Prism of Belief, the resistance pieces as the caps need them, and Saitha's Spear before the first bosses; at the prices seen, the whole rung costs well under one divine.

source.ref: the build's engine first, then damage, then defences; prices m-* in prices[] (2026-10-29)

anoint.reason: 15% increased Magnitude of Bleeding you inflict and 25% increased Physical Damage, on Rake's bleed and the walls' alike: measured on n, Rake 335,029 to 363,901 against map monsters (+9%) and PoB's boss figure 468,725 to 502,575, with EHP unchanged, which carries the boss estimate (boss_n) over the 250,000 floor; it sits 14 points from the tree (past two jewel sockets and two spell-critical small passives), so the amulet takes it with no path

groups.label: Shield Wall
groups.countReason: two walls (Shield Wall's 'Limit 2 active Shield Walls', gem lookup) shattered together by one Fortifying Cry or Thunderous Leap: two hits land, but only the top bleed applies (one bleed per enemy; the brainstorm gate's interview, interviews/brainstorm-1.md), which the record's Count rule follows by counting the hit twice and the bleed once

engagement.reason: Rake's dash ends in melee range of the pack it slashes, and the walls go up beside the boss before the leap lands on it

boss.note: Raise two Shield Walls beside the boss, then Thunderous Leap onto it: the slam shatters both walls (two hits, one bleed, 140% more) and detonates any Rapid Assault spearheads. Swap to Saitha's Spear and stab with Rapid Assault to aggravate the wall's bleed and leave a spearhead, swap back, raise the next pair. Fortifying Cry shatters a pair whenever its 8 s cooldown is up, triggering Shield Wave and granting Guard. Rake fills the gaps. One bleed per enemy, only the top one deals damage: the wall's bleed while it runs, Rake's in the gaps, never the sum; shattering one wall at a time with Leap refreshes the bleed where a pair adds only a second hit

earned.uptime: map packs walk and run at you while Rake's bleed ticks on them, so most of a bleed counts as moving (an estimate); a pack that stops loses the extra 100% unless Herald of Blood's 59% aggravation lands; on a standing boss the same 100% comes from aggravation, Saitha's Spear's Rapid Assault stabs
Brutality III's 20% chance per hit to ignore physical damage reduction, averaged over hits as PoB does by default

3 Rage per melee hit on each enemy struck (Bestial Rage and its two Rage on Hit small passives), so the 30 cap fills in a pack's first strikes and holds while you keep hitting; it starts draining 4 s after the last hit (BaseRageLossDelayMs 4000), so a long walk between packs restarts it

customMods.reason: Shield Wall's '100% more Damage if destroyed by your Skills' plus 40% from its 20% quality (gem lookup 'Shield Wall'; Data/Skills/act_str.lua), which PoB has no stat map for (check_model_coverage gems Shield Wall: possibly unmodelled); every wall here is shattered by Fortifying Cry or Thunderous Leap, your own Warcry and Slam, so the line holds on each wall; the 80% less when an enemy breaks it inside 0.5 s is left out, a risk

Rake's own 'Deals up to 130% more Damage, based on the distance travelled' (100% plus 30% from 20% quality; gem lookup 'Rake'), which PoB applies none of: its stat map names base_dash_additional_damage_from_distance_+%_final while the gem carries base_additional_damage_from_distance_+%_final (Data/Skills/act_dex.lua:6428-6442; the card's skill-shape probe, check 8). Worked out on PoB's own ramp for the line, full at 50 units (5 m, the dash's base_melee_dash_range 50), at PoB's default enemy distance of 20 units (Modules/ConfigOptions.lua:1621): 20/50 x 130% = 52%. A dash from further pays up to 130%, one from beside the enemy nothing

Momentum's 'After moving at least 2 metres during a single use of a Supported Skill, the rest of that use deals 40% more Damage' (gem lookup 'Momentum'), which PoB never applies to Rake: its config option 'Moved 2m during Skill use?' shows only for skills usable while moving (Modules/ConfigOptions.lua:484), and Rake isn't one (the card's dead-slot audit, check 5). Rake's slash comes after its dash, so a dash of 2 m or more earns the 40%; at the 2 m average the distance line above assumes, about half the uses reach it: 40% x 0.5 = 20% (an estimate; needs in-game testing)

claims.text: Tribal Fury (750) carries the clear: its 'Strikes deal Splash Damage' makes Rake, a Strike, hit the target's neighbours, and each splash hit leaves Blood Loss through Atziri's Acuity for the Heralds' explosions. PoB ignores the line, so node power counts the notable as travel; the splash's gain is unmeasured and needs in-game testing.

claims.text: Bestial Rage (10873) and its two Rage on Hit passives (47790, 17625) supply the 30 Rage the configuration counts on: 1 Rage on Melee Hit each, 3 a hit, and Bestial Rage's 12% increased Physical Damage per 10 Rage. Node power can't see the supply, because the Rage count is an earned configuration value that stays set without the nodes.

claims.text: The nine attribute passives set to Dexterity hold the Dexterity that Rake, Thunderous Leap and Rapid Assault require, reached only with the gear's Dexterity lines beside them; node power ranks damage and life alone, so it would move these points and leave the requirement unmet.

The twenty-seven attribute passives set to Strength hold the Strength that Shield Wall, Fortifying Cry and the armour bases require; node power ranks damage and life alone, so it would move these points and leave the requirements unmet.

Doomsayer (57190) gives Herald skills 25% increased Area of Effect and 30% increased damage: the wider explosions carry the Heralds' Blood Loss chain across a pack, clear area PoB can't value, since it models neither Herald's share of the exploded enemy's Blood Loss nor the chain, so node power sees only the explosion's small damage.

Blood Magic (51749) turns every skill's mana cost into a life cost, so Rake's cost per second comes out of life, which Atziri's Acuity's leech refills while hits land; without it Rake's cost outruns the mana the build regenerates and leeches, a sustain node power doesn't measure.

The two Bleed Chance passives (43778, 36894: 5% chance to inflict Bleeding on Hit each, more under Hulking Form) and Bleed Damage (33137) give Thunderous Leap its own bleed, a boss-rotation entry; Rake and the walls bleed on every hit already, so node power's map figure sees nothing in them, and the tree keeps them for the leap's bleed against a boss.

From the budget rung, upgrade in this order: the +4 spear first (the dearest piece, about 50 divines, and the base of every damage line; keep its Dexterity, as on b), then Prism of Belief at +3, the +3 amulet, the body armour and boots with armour applying to elemental damage, the belt, and the rings and Rubies last; the top-roll Ruby had a single listing, so two sockets wait on new ones.

source.ref: Rake's levels and base damage first, then the EHP pieces; prices n-* in prices[] (2026-10-29)
